title: Rework request multiplexer to reduce tail latency and memory churn
creator: Liam Chen
description: The console backend's request multiplexer (internal 'mux' path) has become a major source of tail latency and heap churn. Three related issues were observed in production: (1) per-request serializer allocations that amplify at 95th/99th percentile under burst, (2) contention in the multiplexer hot loop when many slow downstream resolvers are in-flight, and (3) inconsistent cache key segmentation for prefixed KV cache lookups leading to cache misses and repeated work. This ticket refactors the multiplexer to a) introduce a pooled serializer/encoder, b) move slow resolver work off the hot path via an async bounded worker queue with backpressure semantics, and c) standardize cache key composition and add optional cache-hint propagation for hot routes. The goal is to cut 95th/99th latency by at least 25% and reduce peak heap allocations during high concurrency scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile end-to-end console API latency reduced by >=25% on staging load test compared to baseline (see performance dashboard link)
Heap allocation spikes during the standard burst profile reduced by >=30% in flamegraphs captured during load tests
No regressions in existing GraphQL resolver outputs; all conformance tests pass (unit + integration)
Cache key composition standardized for top 10 console routes and cache-hint header is propagated for eligible responses
Instrumented metrics added: mux.queue_depth, mux.worker_rejections, serializer.pool_reuse_pct and dashboard updated
implementation_plan: Benchmark and reproduce baseline in staging using existing load script (perf/load-scenarios/console-burst)
Introduce serializer pool (sync.Pool equivalent) and replace per-request allocations; measure reuse rate
Refactor mux hot loop: extract resolver invocation into non-blocking submit to bounded async worker pool with configurable concurrency and FIFO backpressure
Add per-route cache key composer utility and migrate top routes to use it; add small compatibility shim for older keys
Add optional 'x-cache-hint' propagation and ensure telemetry records hits/misses with new key format
Run schema/contract tests and end-to-end smoke tests; update rollout plan to canary new mux path on 5% of traffic
Submit PR, request design/PM review for any API surface changes, and schedule staged rollout with rollback instrumentation
progress_updates: 2026-02-21: Spike completed to validate serializer pooling reduces allocations locally (measured ~40% fewer allocations during synthetic burst). Notes in the design doc: https://confluence.redwood/example-mux-pool

2026-02-27: Prototype worker-pool implemented in feature branch eng/75321-mux-pool. Early tests show queue depth stabilizes under memory pressure but throughput drops with naive single-worker-per-request approach
2026-03-03: Decided on bounded async worker queue with per-route concurrency caps after PM/Infra discussion; added config knobs for dedicated capacity vs hosted tier
2026-03-07: Standardized cache key spec v2 drafted; compatibility shim planned for 2 weeks to avoid mass invalidation. PR for key composer: github.com/redwood/console/pull/9832
2026-03-10: Integration tests added for serializer pool; found race when pool items reused across goroutine-local buffers — fixed by adding small reset() routine on checkout
2026-03-11: Begin staging load tests with mux feature gate enabled on a replica set. Observed initial 95th latency drop ~18% and allocation reduction ~28% — further tuning planned
notes: Design trade-offs: pushing resolver work off the hot path improves tail latency but makes error TTL semantics more complex; chosen to surface partial failures via the standard async-error wrapper used elsewhere in platform
We considered adopting a global request coalescer but rejected due to cross-tenant interference and complexity with private deployments
Follow-up work: extend pool to handle encoder variants for streaming responses, and explore pre-warming for Dedicated instances
risk_mitigation: Canary rollout with feature flag at 5% traffic; automatic rollback if mux.worker_rejections > 1% or mux.queue_depth > configured threshold for >10m. Add extensive logging for first-of-kind errors and correlate with tracing ids. Keep compatibility shim for old cache keys for 2 weeks before migrating live routes.
qa_plan: Unit tests for serializer pool lifecycle and reset behavior
Integration tests that simulate slow resolvers and verify backpressure semantics and error propagation
Staging load test with 3x baseline burst and full flamegraph capture
Canary verification checklist: latency regressions, error rates, queue metrics, memory profiles
